title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

learn.hook: One equation, two unknowns — and endless answers! Find out why one equation alone can't pin down the price of a samosa.
points: A linear equation in two variables can be written as ax + by + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a and b are not both zero.
A solution is a pair (x, y) that makes the equation true. One such equation has infinitely many solutions.
All the solutions of one linear equation lie on a straight line when plotted on a graph.
Real situations — prices at a mela, ages, marks, money — often give two unknowns linked by a fact. Each fact becomes one equation.

steps: We could keep going for ever — there are infinitely many solutions

learn.reallife: At a school fete, '2 cups of chai and 3 samosas cost ₹70' is one linear equation in two variables — you need a second fact to find each price.

games.title: Linear in two variables or not?
True or false?
items: x + y = 10 has exactly one solution.
The graph of 2x − y = 3 is a straight line.
Every linear equation in two variables gives a straight line.
In ax + by + c = 0, a and b can both be 0.
Then there would be no variable left; a and b cannot both be zero.
'Riya is 4 years older than Kabir' can be written as r = k + 4.
Riya's age r equals Kabir's age k plus 4.

quiz.q: Which of these is a linear equation in two variables?
quiz.explain: 2x + 3y = 7 has two variables, each with power 1. x² + y has a square, xy is a product of variables, and 3x + 5 = 11 has only one variable.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any equation with x and y in it is linear

quiz.q: When 3x = 2y − 5 is written as ax + by + c = 0, what are a, b and c?
quiz.explain: Move everything to the left: 3x − 2y + 5 = 0. So a = 3, b = −2 and c = 5.
quiz.mistake: Moves terms across without changing their signs

quiz.q: Is (2, 1) a solution of 3x − 4y = 2?
options: No, because x must be bigger than y
quiz.explain: Put x = 2 and y = 1: 6 − 4 = 2, which matches the right side, so it is a solution.
quiz.mistake: Swaps x and y, or adds the coordinates instead of substituting

quiz.q: How many solutions does the single equation x + 2y = 6 have?
quiz.explain: For every value of x you can find a matching y, so there are infinitely many solutions. They all lie on one straight line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one equation is enough to find both unknowns

quiz.q: For x + y = 7, what is y when x = 3?
quiz.explain: 3 + y = 7, so y = 4. (3, 4) is one of the many solutions.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 7 instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Ravi's age is 5 years more than twice Priya's age. If Ravi is x years old and Priya y years old, which equation fits?
quiz.explain: Twice Priya's age is 2y; 5 more than that is 2y + 5, and this equals Ravi's age x.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up whose age is doubled

quiz.q: At a mela, 2 pens and 3 notebooks cost ₹70. If a pen costs ₹x and a notebook ₹y, which equation shows this?
quiz.explain: 2 pens cost 2x and 3 notebooks cost 3y. Together they cost ₹70, so 2x + 3y = 70.
quiz.mistake: Matches the numbers to the wrong items

quiz.q: Which point lies on the line 2x − y = 4?
quiz.mistake: Substitutes the coordinates the wrong way round

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Why can't one equation like x + y = 10 tell me both x and y?' Explain to Gappu.
teach.praise: Chirp! One equation has endless solutions on a line — I need a second equation to find the one answer!
teach.nudge: So how many solutions does one equation have, and what do I need to find just one?

learn.hook: Two straight lines on a graph can meet once, never meet, or sit right on top of each other — and each story tells you about the answer!
points: A pair of linear equations is a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0. Each one is a straight line on a graph.
If the lines intersect at one point, that point is the unique solution. The pair is consistent.
If the lines are parallel, there is no solution. The pair is inconsistent.
If the lines coincide (are the same line), there are infinitely many solutions. The pair is dependent and consistent.
Shortcut without drawing: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂ means one solution; a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂ means parallel lines; a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂ means the lines coincide.

example.q: Solve x + y = 5 and x − y = 1 graphically.
steps: For x + y = 5, plot (0, 5) and (5, 0) and join them
For x − y = 1, plot (1, 0) and (0, −1) and join them

learn.reallife: If two auto-rickshaw fare plans are drawn as lines, the crossing point shows the distance at which both plans cost the same.

games.title: Lines on a graph
items: A pair of parallel lines has no common solution.
Parallel lines never meet, so no point lies on both.
If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂, the two lines coincide.
One equation is just a multiple of the other, so they are the same line.
An inconsistent pair has exactly one solution.
Inconsistent means there is no solution at all.
x + y = 3 and 2x + 2y = 6 have infinitely many solutions.
The second equation is 2 times the first, so the lines coincide.
Two different straight lines can meet at exactly two points.
Two different straight lines meet at most once.
The pair x = 3 and y = 2 has the unique solution (3, 2).
x = 3 is a vertical line and y = 2 is a horizontal line; they cross only at (3, 2).

quiz.q: The lines 2x + 3y = 9 and 4x + 6y = 18 are…
quiz.explain: 2/4 = 3/6 = 9/18 = 1/2. All three ratios are equal, so the lines coincide.
quiz.mistake: Sees equal a and b ratios and says parallel without checking c

quiz.q: For which values of k do kx + 2y = 5 and 3x + y = 1 have a unique solution?
quiz.explain: A unique solution needs a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, so k/3 ≠ 2/1, which means k ≠ 6.
quiz.mistake: Uses '=' instead of '≠' for the unique-solution condition

quiz.q: For what value of k are the lines x + 2y = 3 and 3x + ky = 7 parallel?
quiz.explain: Parallel lines need 1/3 = 2/k, so k = 6. Also 3/7 ≠ 1/3, so the lines do not coincide.
quiz.mistake: Cross-multiplies wrongly and gets 2/3

quiz.q: The lines x + y = 6 and x − y = 2 are drawn on a graph. Where do they meet?
quiz.explain: Adding the equations gives 2x = 8, so x = 4 and y = 2. Check: 4 + 2 = 6 and 4 − 2 = 2.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the x- and y-coordinates

quiz.q: Riya draws two lines that never meet, however far she extends them. The pair of equations is…
quiz.explain: Lines that never meet are parallel, so there is no solution. Such a pair is called inconsistent.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the words consistent and inconsistent

quiz.q: Where does the line 2x + y = 6 meet the y-axis?
quiz.explain: On the y-axis x = 0, so y = 6. The point is (0, 6).
quiz.mistake: Finds where the line meets the x-axis instead, (3, 0)

quiz.q: How many solutions do 3x − 5y = 2 and 6x − 10y = 4 have?
quiz.explain: 3/6 = −5/−10 = 2/4 = 1/2, so the lines coincide and every point on the line is a solution.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a pair of linear equations always has exactly one solution

quiz.q: Which pair has exactly one solution?
quiz.explain: For x + y = 5 and 2x − y = 1, a₁/a₂ = 1/2 and b₁/b₂ = 1/(−1) = −1 are different, so the lines intersect once (at (2, 3)).
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the ratios a₁/a₂ and b₁/b₂

teach.ask: Gappu draws two lines with a crayon: 'How do these lines tell me how many answers the equations have?'
teach.praise: Cheep! Meeting once, never meeting, or being the same line — I get it now!
teach.nudge: What happens to the answer if the lines are parallel, or the same line?

topics.title: Making lines and solving word problems on a graph

learn.hook: Can you invent a line that never meets yours — or one that sits exactly on top of it? Ratios make it easy!
points: Given a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0: for an INTERSECTING line, choose a₂ and b₂ so that a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂.
For a PARALLEL line, multiply only a₁ and b₁ by the same number and pick a different constant, so a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂.
For a COINCIDENT line, multiply the whole equation by the same non-zero number.
A line meets the x-axis where y = 0. To find the triangle made by two lines and the x-axis, use the two x-axis points and the point where the lines meet.
Word problems: name the unknowns, write one equation for each fact, draw both lines and read where they meet.

example.q: Solve x + y = 5 and 2x − y = 4 graphically and find the triangle formed by these lines and the x-axis.
steps: The lines meet at (3, 2) — check: 3 + 2 = 5 and 6 − 2 = 4 ✓
The triangle has vertices (3, 2), (5, 0) and (2, 0). Base = 3, height = 2, area = ½ × 3 × 2 = 3 sq units
example.answer: Solution x = 3, y = 2; triangle with vertices (3, 2), (5, 0), (2, 0)

learn.reallife: City planners draw roads as lines on a map — parallel roads never meet, crossing roads meet at a junction. That's exactly this topic.

games.title: Match the line to its partner with 2x + 3y − 8 = 0
Solving a word problem graphically
items: Name the two unknowns, x and y
Write one equation for each fact in the story
Make a table of points for each equation
Plot both lines on the same graph
Read the point where the lines meet and check it in the story

quiz.q: Which line is parallel to 2x + 3y − 8 = 0?
quiz.explain: For 4x + 6y − 5 = 0: a₁/a₂ = 2/4 = 1/2 and b₁/b₂ = 3/6 = 1/2, but c₁/c₂ = −8/−5 = 8/5 ≠ 1/2. So the lines are parallel.
quiz.mistake: Picks the line that is just the same equation multiplied (that one coincides)

quiz.q: Which line coincides with 2x + 3y − 8 = 0?
quiz.explain: 6x + 9y − 24 = 0 is 3 × (2x + 3y − 8) = 0, so all three ratios are 1/3 and the lines are the same.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies a and b but not c

quiz.q: Which line intersects x − 2y + 4 = 0 at exactly one point?
quiz.explain: For 2x + y − 3 = 0: a₁/a₂ = 1/2 but b₁/b₂ = −2/1 = −2. The ratios differ, so the lines cross once. The others are parallel or coincident.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare a₁/a₂ with b₁/b₂

quiz.q: The lines x + y = 5 and 2x − y = 4 are drawn on a graph. Where do they meet?
quiz.explain: Adding the equations gives 3x = 9, so x = 3 and y = 2. Both lines pass through (3, 2).
quiz.mistake: Swaps x and y or gives an x-axis point instead

quiz.q: Where does the line 2x − y = 4 meet the x-axis?
quiz.explain: On the x-axis y = 0, so 2x = 4 and x = 2. The point is (2, 0).
quiz.mistake: Puts x = 0 instead of y = 0 (that gives the y-axis point)

quiz.q: The lines x + y = 5 and 2x − y = 4 and the x-axis form a triangle with vertices (3, 2), (5, 0) and (2, 0). What is its area?
quiz.explain: Base along the x-axis = 5 − 2 = 3, height = y-coordinate of (3, 2) = 2. Area = ½ × 3 × 2 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ½ in the triangle area formula

quiz.q: 10 students of Class X took part in a maths quiz. The number of girls is 4 more than the number of boys. How many girls took part?
quiz.explain: Let girls = x and boys = y: x + y = 10 and x − y = 4. The lines meet at (7, 3), so 7 girls.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of boys, or adds 10 and 4

quiz.q: Half the perimeter of a rectangular garden is 36 m, and its length is 4 m more than its width. What is the width?
quiz.explain: l + w = 36 and l − w = 4. Subtracting gives 2w = 32, so w = 16 m (and l = 20 m).
quiz.mistake: Gives the length instead of the width

teach.ask: Gappu wants to draw a line that never meets 2x + 3y = 8, and another that lies exactly on top of it. Explain how.
teach.praise: Tweet! Multiply only x and y parts for a parallel line, and the whole equation for a coincident one!
teach.nudge: But what do I change to make the line parallel instead of the same line?

learn.hook: Make one variable 'wear the costume' of the other, swap it in, and the puzzle shrinks to one variable!
points: Step 1: from one equation, write one variable in terms of the other (for example y = 2x − 4).
Step 2: substitute this into the other equation, so it has only one variable.
Step 3: solve that equation, then put the value back to find the other variable.
Always check your answer in both original equations.
If you end with a true statement like 6 = 6, there are infinitely many solutions. If you get a false one like 0 = 4, there is no solution.

example.q: Kabir buys 2 pens and 3 notebooks for ₹80. A notebook costs ₹10 more than a pen. Find each price.
steps: Let a pen cost ₹p and a notebook ₹n. Then n = p + 10 and 2p + 3n = 80

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers in a market use this kind of reasoning when one price is 'so much more' than another.

games.title: Put the substitution steps in order

items.q: y = 2x and x + y = 9. Find x
y = x + 1 and x + y = 7. Find y
x = 2y and x + y = 15. Find x
y = 3x and x + y = 8. Find y
x = y + 2 and x + y = 10. Find x
y = 5 − x and 2x + y = 8. Find x

quiz.q: Solve x + y = 10 and x − y = 2. What is x?
quiz.explain: From x − y = 2, x = y + 2. Then (y + 2) + y = 10, so y = 4 and x = 6.
quiz.mistake: Gives the value of y instead of x

quiz.q: If y = 2x − 3 and 3x + y = 12, what is x?
quiz.explain: 3x + (2x − 3) = 12 gives 5x = 15, so x = 3 (and y = 3).
quiz.mistake: Moves −3 across without changing its sign, getting 5x = 9

quiz.q: Substituting y = 4 − x into 2x + 3y = 10 gives which equation?
quiz.explain: 3y = 3(4 − x) = 12 − 3x, so the equation becomes 2x + 12 − 3x = 10.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the first term inside the bracket by 3

quiz.q: Meena is 3 times as old as her brother. The sum of their ages is 24 years. How old is Meena?
quiz.explain: Let the brother be b years. Meena = 3b, so 3b + b = 24, b = 6 and Meena is 18.
quiz.mistake: Gives the brother's age instead of Meena's

quiz.q: 2 samosas and 1 cup of tea cost ₹40. 1 samosa and 1 cup of tea cost ₹25. What does one samosa cost?
quiz.explain: From the second equation t = 25 − s. Then 2s + 25 − s = 40, so s = 15 (and tea costs ₹10).
quiz.mistake: Gives the price of the tea

quiz.q: While solving a pair by substitution, Aisha ends up with 6 = 6. What does this mean?
options: The pair has infinitely many solutions
quiz.explain: A statement that is always true means both equations describe the same line, so every point on it is a solution.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number 6 is the value of a variable

quiz.q: While solving a pair, Arjun's working ends with 0 = 4. What does this tell him?
options: The pair has infinitely many solutions
quiz.explain: 0 = 4 is false, so no values of x and y satisfy both equations. The lines are parallel.
quiz.mistake: Reads the numbers in a false statement as the solution

quiz.q: Two numbers add up to 35 and one is 7 more than the other. What is the larger number?
quiz.explain: Let the smaller be x. Then x + (x + 7) = 35, so x = 14 and the larger is 21.
quiz.mistake: Gives the smaller number, or just halves 35

teach.ask: Gappu has two equations and is stuck: 'How does the substitution trick work?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Write one in terms of the other, put it in, and solve. Easy-peasy!
teach.nudge: After I write y in terms of x, where do I put it?

learn.hook: Line up two equations, add or subtract, and watch one variable vanish like a magic trick!
points: Multiply one or both equations so that one variable has the same (or opposite) coefficient in both.
Subtract the equations if the coefficients are the same, or add them if they are opposite, to eliminate that variable.
Solve for the remaining variable, then substitute back to find the other one.
For word problems: name the two unknowns, write two equations from the two facts given, then solve.
Check that your answer makes sense in the story — a negative number of notes is a sign of an error!

steps: The y terms are +2y and −2y, so add the equations

learn.reallife: Cricket kit shops, fruit sellers and ticket counters all face 'two unknown prices, two bills' puzzles like these.

items.text: To eliminate y from 2x + 3y = 8 and x − y = 1, multiply the second equation by ___
Adding x + y = 7 and x − y = 3 gives 2x = ___
Subtracting x + y = 5 from x + 2y = 9 gives y = ___

games.title: Match the story to its equations
pairs: Two numbers add to 50 and differ by 10
A fraction's numerator and denominator add to 12; the denominator is twice the numerator
A bat costs ₹300 more than a ball; together they cost ₹500

quiz.q: Solve 2x + y = 7 and x − y = 2. What is y?
quiz.explain: Adding the equations gives 3x = 9, so x = 3. Then y = 7 − 2 × 3 = 1.
quiz.mistake: Stops after finding x and gives it as y

quiz.q: Solve 3x + 4y = 10 and 3x − 2y = 4. What is x?
quiz.explain: Subtract: (3x + 4y) − (3x − 2y) = 6y = 6, so y = 1. Then 3x = 10 − 4 = 6, so x = 2.
quiz.mistake: Treats 4y − (−2y) as 2y instead of 6y

quiz.q: Which step eliminates x from x + 3y = 9 and 2x + y = 8?
options: Multiply the second equation by 3 and add
Multiply the first equation by 2 and subtract
Subtract the equations as they are
quiz.explain: Multiplying the first by 2 gives 2x + 6y = 18. Subtracting 2x + y = 8 removes x: 5y = 10.
quiz.mistake: Adds or subtracts before making the x coefficients equal

quiz.q: Harpreet has 25 notes of ₹10 and ₹20 worth ₹350 in all. How many ₹20 notes does she have?
quiz.explain: x + y = 25 and 10x + 20y = 350, so x + 2y = 35. Subtracting gives y = 10 ₹20 notes (and 15 ₹10 notes).
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of ₹10 notes instead

quiz.q: 2 cricket bats and 3 balls cost ₹1300. 1 bat and 2 balls cost ₹700. What does one bat cost?
quiz.explain: Double the second bill: 2b + 4c = 1400. Subtract the first: c = 100. Then b = 700 − 200 = 500.
quiz.mistake: Gives the price of a ball

quiz.q: The numerator and denominator of a fraction add up to 13, and the denominator is 3 more than the numerator. What is the fraction?
quiz.explain: x + y = 13 and y − x = 3. Adding gives 2y = 16, so y = 8 and x = 5. The fraction is 5/8.
quiz.mistake: Writes the fraction upside down

quiz.q: The digits of a two-digit number add up to 9. Reversing the digits increases the number by 27. What is the number?
quiz.explain: Let the number be 10a + b. Then a + b = 9 and (10b + a) − (10a + b) = 27, so b − a = 3. Solving: b = 6, a = 3, giving 36. Check: 63 − 36 = 27 ✓
quiz.mistake: Gives the reversed number 63

quiz.q: Solve 4x + 3y = 26 and 2x − 3y = 4. What is x + y?
quiz.explain: Adding gives 6x = 30, so x = 5. Then 3y = 26 − 20 = 6, so y = 2. x + y = 7.
quiz.mistake: Gives only x (5) instead of x + y

teach.ask: Gappu stares at 3x + 2y = 11 and 2x − 2y = 4: 'How can I make one letter disappear?'
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Make the numbers match, add or subtract, and one letter vanishes. Magic!
teach.nudge: What must be the same in both equations before I add or subtract them?

topics.title: Choosing a method and chapter recap

learn.hook: A graph says the answer is 'about 1.4'. Algebra says it is exactly 7/5. Which would you trust in an exam?
points: Graphs are hard to read when the answer is a fraction or decimal like (1.4, 2.6), so we use algebraic methods for exact answers.
Substitution is handy when one variable already has coefficient 1 (like x = 3y + 1). Elimination is handy when the coefficients can be matched easily.
In elimination, if BOTH variables disappear: a true statement (0 = 0) means infinitely many solutions; a false one (0 = 3) means no solution.
Both methods always give the same answer. Once you have (x, y), you can use it to find an unknown constant, like m in y = mx + 5.
Recap: unique solution (intersecting lines), no solution (parallel), infinitely many (coincident); check by ratios or by algebra.

example.q: Solve x + y = 5 and x − y = 1, and hence find m if y = mx + 5.

learn.reallife: GPS apps solve equations exactly instead of 'reading a map by eye' — just like we use algebra instead of guessing from a graph.

games.title: What does the final line tell you?

quiz.q: Why do we need algebraic methods when we can already solve pairs of equations on a graph?
options: Graphs give only rough readings when the solution is like (1.4, 2.6)
Algebra works only for parallel lines
Graphs work only for word problems
quiz.explain: Reading a point such as (7/5, 13/5) from a graph is not accurate. Algebra gives the exact values.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the graph method is wrong rather than just imprecise

quiz.q: Solve x + y = 5 and x − y = 1. If the solution also satisfies y = mx + 5, what is m?
quiz.explain: The solution is x = 3, y = 2. Then 2 = 3m + 5, so 3m = −3 and m = −1.
quiz.mistake: Makes a sign slip when moving 5 across

quiz.q: Eliminating from 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + 6y = 10 gives 0 = 0. What does this mean?
quiz.explain: Doubling the first equation gives the second, so they are the same line. 0 = 0 is always true: infinitely many solutions.
quiz.mistake: Reads 0 = 0 as x = 0, y = 0

quiz.q: Doubling 3x − y = 2 and subtracting it from 6x − 2y = 7 gives 0 = 3. What does this tell you?
options: The lines are parallel, so there is no solution
quiz.explain: Both variables vanished and we got a false statement, so the lines are parallel and never meet.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any final number is the value of x

quiz.q: Priya solves 3x + 2y = 12 and 5x − 2y = 4 by elimination, and Aman solves the same pair by substitution. What value of y should BOTH of them get?
quiz.explain: Elimination: adding gives 8x = 16, so x = 2 and y = 3. Substitution: from the first equation y = (12 − 3x)/2; putting this in the second gives 5x − (12 − 3x) = 4, so 8x = 16, x = 2 and y = 3. Both methods give the same answer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks different methods can give different answers, or gives x instead of y

quiz.q: Solve y = 2x and 3x + y = 15 by substitution. What is y?
quiz.explain: Substitute y = 2x: 3x + 2x = 15, so x = 3 and y = 2 × 3 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Gives the value of x instead of y

quiz.q: For x = 3y + 1 and 2x + 5y = 13, which method is quickest, and what is the solution?
quiz.explain: x is already alone, so substitute: 2(3y + 1) + 5y = 13 → 11y = 11 → y = 1 and x = 4.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the values of x and y

quiz.q: Recap: if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, what can you say about the pair of equations?
options: Inconsistent — the lines are parallel and there is no solution
quiz.explain: Equal x- and y-ratios but a different constant ratio means the lines have the same slope but different positions: parallel, no solution.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the parallel and coincident conditions

teach.ask: Gappu solved a pair by elimination and was left with 0 = 0. He is confused. What does it mean, and when should he use substitution instead?
teach.praise: Chirp! 0 = 0 means the same line — endless answers. And substitution is great when a variable is already alone!
teach.nudge: And what if he had got 0 = 3 instead?
